review: 1:2 חֹמֶר אָנֹכִי בְּיָדֶךָ — 'clay am I in Your hand' (Jer 18:6, כַּחֹמֶר בְּיַד הַיּוֹצֵר); the Arabic خَزَفٌ إِنِّي بَيْنَ يَدَيْك is that verse, and חֹמֶר is the potter's word.
1:3 עַצֵּב חַיַּי — 'shape my life'; the Arabic كَيِّفْ حَيَاتِي is 'fashion', and עָצַב in the piel is used of forming (Job 10:8, עִצַּבְתַּנִי).
1:1–1:1 repeated at the head of all three stanzas — the Arabic repeats أَنْجِزْ يَا رَبِّي قَصْدَكَ بِي verbatim, so the Hebrew repeats it rather than varying for elegance.

3:4 לְמַעַן יָצִיץ בִּי הַמָּשִׁיחַ — 'that Christ may blossom in me'; the Arabic كَيْ يَتَجَلَّى فِيَّ الْمَسِيح is 'be revealed in me', and צוּץ ('blossom') keeps the growth image while fitting the line.
